NBA Front Office FAQ: rosters, trades and getting fired
Are the rosters real?

The players are real, about ten curated per franchise. Contracts, salaries and ages in the sim are explicitly fictional.

Why did my trade get rejected?

The engine values rating adjusted for age and wants to come out ahead. Offer youth, take back age, or add a pick.

Can I get fired?

Yes. Ownership grades the mandate every season and tracks trust from 0 to 100. Losing the play-in when the ask was a banner costs real trust, a luxury tax bill costs a point per 6 million of it, and at zero the save ends and you take another job.

What happens if I start the season with 12 players?

The league fills you to 14 at tip off with the lowest rated free agents in the pool on one year minimum deals, 2 million each, and the feed names them. Sign who you actually want before you press play. With 16 or more you cannot start until you waive down to 15.

Does my save persist?

Yes, the league auto saves in your browser across unlimited seasons. Clearing site data wipes the franchise.

Is NBA Front Office free to play?

Yes. NBA Front Office is free to play on DoUKnowBall, right in your browser. No download and no signup needed.

NBA Front Office rules: the cap, trades and the play in
Cap room and roster size limits
The cap starts at the real 2026-27 figure, just under 165 million, and rises 7 percent every season in the game. You can waive down to 8 players during the year, but the season cannot tip off with fewer than 14 or more than 15: short of 14 the league fills the gap with minimum deals at 2 million each and tells you who, and above 15 the first round waits until you waive down.
The luxury tax, the aprons and the repeater rate
The real league put its 2026-27 tax line at 200.4 million, but the salaries here are the game's own and run richer at the top, so every new league sets its line from its own payrolls instead: enough clubs over it to look like a real season (eight paid tax in 2023-24), but nobody facing a bill above 190 million, about the most any club has ever been billed. MLB Front Office rules for the tax line, trades and trust
The tax line and its hard cap
The tax line starts at 244 million, matching the real 2026 threshold, and it is a hard cap, rising 3 percent a season.
How the playoff format is seeded
Playoffs use the real format: best-of-3 Wild Card, best-of-5 Division Series, best-of-7 LCS and World Series.
What trades weigh most
Trades weigh rating, age and position, with premiums on aces, shortstops and catchers.
DRAFT PICKS AND SCOUTING ERROR
You hold 2 picks a year, and scout grades carry error. True ratings show only after you pick.
Injuries and automatic franchise saves
Injuries cost one to four rounds on the IL, and your franchise saves automatically.
Designating a player and the dead money
A DFA is not free. Half the man's salary stays on this season's payroll as dead money, a quarter lands on next season's if he had years left, and you cannot sign him back until the offseason.
Trust upstairs and getting fired
Trust upstairs runs 0 to 100: beat the mandate and it climbs, miss it and it falls, a ring fixes almost anything, and at zero you are fired and the save ends.
MLB Front Office walkthrough: a division title, then a scouting miss
Trading an aging ace for a young shortstop

You take a club 8 million under the line. A DFA clears a bloated deal, the savings sign a 79 rated reliever, and your aging ace becomes a 26 year old shortstop.

Winning the division, losing the LCS in six

You win the division, take the bye, and still lose the LCS in six. Next spring your 84 grade pick arrives as an 80. Scouts, man.

MLB Front Office tips for payroll, age and October depth
Treating payroll room as a roster spot
Payroll room is a roster spot. One dumped albatross often buys two useful arms.
Why age drives value
Age drives value. A decent 24 year old can outpull a 33 year old star, so sell veterans early.
Spending on lineup first, then pitching
The sim weighs your lineup most, then rotation, then bullpen. Spend in that order.
Building for repeat October trips
October is a variance machine, so build for repeat trips, not one all-in year.
MLB Front Office FAQ: contracts, the tax line and trades
Are the contracts real?

Rosters and ratings come from real data, but every salary, contract and transaction in the sim is fictional.

Can I go over the tax line?

No. Moves that break the line do not go through. That squeeze is most of the job.

Why did my trade get rejected?

The AI wants a premium on rating, age and position. Add one of your 2 picks, or offer someone younger.

Can I get fired?

Yes. Ownership grades the mandate every season and tracks trust from 0 to 100. A 70 win season on a win-the-World-Series payroll costs real trust, and at zero the save ends and you take another job.
